name: UGC 7356 (Hubble)
blurb: UGC 7356, a nucleated dwarf elliptical galaxy, seen by Hubble.
label: ugc07356-hubble
story: A smooth, faint dwarf galaxy with a central nucleus, lying close on the sky to NGC 4258, near one of its spiral arms. Hubble came here in a survey of the dwarf-galaxy-rich Canes Venatici I region, gauging distances from the brightest red giant stars.

claims.text: UGC 7356 is a classical nucleated dwarf elliptical
UGC 7356 is close in projection to NGC 4258
UGC 7356 lies near the southern spiral arm of NGC 4258
UGC 7356 is a target of program 10905, a survey of the dwarf-galaxy-rich Canes Venatici I region
The program measures distances using the tip of the red giant branch
